[{"content":"You are a teaching assistant analyzing a teacher's audio transcript about student observations.

Your task:
1. Identify which students are mentioned in the transcript
2. Match each mentioned name to the student roster below (handle phonetic/partial matches)
3. Extract the date if mentioned (format YYYY-MM-DD), otherwise leave empty
4. Write a summary per student capturing what the teacher said about them
   - Clean up speech artifacts (false starts, filler words, repetitions) into clear sentences
   - Preserve the teacher's voice, tone, and specific observations — do NOT add details or opinions not present in the transcript
   - Keep the teacher's vocabulary and perspective (first person if they used it)
   - Combine multiple mentions of the same student into a cohesive note

Student Roster:
- Emma Torres (class_name Class A)
- Ryan Mitchell (class_name Class A)
- Lila Patel (class_name Class A)

Rules:
- Match mentioned names against the roster even if pronunciation differs slightly
- Some roster entries include "(aka ...)" aliases — if a teacher uses an alias, match it to the canonical name and return the canonical name in the "name" field
- Set confidence 0.0-1.0 for each match. Use >= 0.7 for confident matches.
- If confidence < 0.7, include up to 3 closest roster matches in "candidates"
- A student is "individually mentioned" ONLY if the teacher uses their name (or a recognizable nickname/variant of their name). Generic group references like "everyone", "all students", "the class" do NOT count as individual mentions.
- Do NOT create entries for students who are never individually mentioned by name. If a student is only covered by group-level observations (e.g. "the class was loud") but never called out by name, they must NOT appear in the output.
- For students who ARE individually mentioned by name, their quoted_text MUST include BOTH their individual observations AND any group-level observations from the same transcript/class. This applies to EVERY individually-mentioned student in that class, regardless of where the group observation appears in the transcript (beginning, middle, or end) or which students were named immediately before/after it. Do not attach group observations only to the students mentioned closest to them — propagate them to all named students in the class.
  Example: Transcript says "Alice did great. Bob was quiet. The whole class struggled with fractions." → BOTH Alice's and Bob's quoted_text must include the fractions observation, not just Bob's.
- If the transcript contains group references like "everyone", "all students", or "the class", apply those observations only to students in the class being discussed, not to ALL classes. Use context clues (class name mentions, prior student mentions) to determine which class is meant.
- For multi-student transcripts, produce a separate entry per student with relevant passages
- If a mentioned student cannot be matched to any roster entry, do not include them in the output
- If no students are clearly mentioned, return an empty students array
- The "class_name" field for each student MUST exactly match one of the class names from the roster above. Do not invent or abbreviate class names.
- IMPORTANT: Clean up speech into readable sentences, but do NOT invent observations or editorialize. Stay faithful to what the teacher actually said.

Yeah, that's, that's about it for today.","role":"user"}]

MOTIVATION AND PARTICIPATION

Chloé generally shows a positive attitude toward classroom activities. She is cooperative with the group and the teacher, as seen when she stopped repeatedly asking for clarification after being reminded. She participates actively in activities, such as the "what's missing" game and worksheet tasks, and enjoys engaging with new material, like the story and vocabulary exercises. However, she sometimes holds back when new content is introduced, requiring additional support with vocabulary cards and story retelling. Her participation is stronger when using familiar structures, such as stating her age and gender, which she does almost always with the correct phrasing.

BEHAVIOUR

Chloé is well-integrated within the group and responds to classroom management strategies, such as the traffic light system. She can be easily distracted or tired, as noted on one occasion, and at times asks repetitive questions even when she knows the answer, which briefly disrupted the flow of the lesson. However, she adjusts her behaviour when reminded and is generally playful and engaged with her peers. The group’s mood occasionally affects her focus, as the class was loud at the start of one session but settled well afterward.

LEARNING

Use of structures: Chloé repeats structures well (e.g., "Emma is wearing...") and uses complete sentences for age and gender. She understands and applies concepts like clean/dirty and dry/wet but needs reminders for full structures in some activities.

Learning objectives: She partially masters clothing vocabulary and needs support with colours. She understands story-related tasks with assistance and enjoys hands-on activities like dressing a character or placing stickers. Her counting skills are strong, and she follows worksheet instructions well.

Strengths:

  • Strong participation in familiar or structured tasks (e.g., age, gender, worksheets).
  • Good repetition of new vocabulary and structures when guided.
  • Engages well with interactive and visual activities (e.g., tattoos, stickers).
  • Responsive to redirection and classroom management techniques.

Areas for improvement:

  • Vocabulary retention: Needs reinforcement with colours and clothing items. Plan: Additional practice with flashcards and pairing exercises.
  • Focus and attention: Occasionally distracted or repetitive in questions. Plan: Targeted reminders to listen fully before asking for clarification.
  • Story comprehension: Requires support to retell stories independently. Plan: Step-by-step scaffolding and repeated exposure to story elements.
The school is committed to addressing these areas through targeted activities and individual support.

MOTIVATION AND PARTICIPATION

Motivation: Chloé generally approaches classroom activities positively. She was in a very good mood in one session, liked the “what’s missing” activity, and was excited to hear more about the new story tattoo. Chloé can be distracted and tired, and she was not always attentive when instructions were being given. Report Card for Chloé – Class Emma · Sat

Motivation and Participation

Chloé demonstrates a mixed attitude toward classroom activities. She shows willingness to engage in tasks she enjoys, such as the what’s missing activity and pairing actions to rooms, where she participated actively and repeated new vocabulary and structures well. However, she occasionally holds back when faced with unfamiliar material, such as colours, clothes vocabulary, and story retelling, where she required significant support. Her cooperation with peers is generally positive—she works well in group tasks (e.g., dressing Emma with Théo’s help) but can become repetitive or distracted, such as when she repeatedly asked where to place items despite knowing the answers, which briefly disrupted the group dynamic.

Chloé’s participation fluctuates based on her confidence with the material. She engages confidently in internalised tasks (e.g., stating her age and gender with complete structures, counting, and worksheet activities) but is hesitant with new content, often requiring prompts or peer assistance (e.g., vocabulary cards, story retelling). Her mood also influences her involvement; on days she is tired or distracted, her focus wanes, leading to frequent questions like “quoi quoi quoi” during instructions.

Behaviour

Chloé is generally well-integrated into the group but can be easily distracted, particularly when tired or when tasks require sustained attention. She responds well to structural reminders (e.g., the traffic light system) and peer feedback (e.g., stopping repetitive questions when Léo reacted). Her behaviour is influenced by the group’s energy—she participates better in a calm environment but struggles when the class is loud or playful. Notably, her mood varies: she was in a “very good mood” on one occasion but “quite distracted and tired” on another, affecting her engagement.

Learning

    • Achieved: States age and gender almost always with complete structures; follows worksheet tasks accurately; counts well; participates in storytime with support.
    • Developing: Vocabulary retention (colours, clothes, body parts) and independent story retelling. She partially understands number songs and tattoo/body-part activities but requires assistance.

    • Strong in repetitive or structured tasks (worksheets, counting, bingo cards).

    • Vocabulary mastery: Focus on colours, clothes, and body-part terms through flashcards and labelling games.

To address this, we will continue to provide targeted support during routines and encourage her to express her needs calmly. The school remains committed to reinforcing her confidence in these areas.

KIDS Report: Camille (Class: Oliver · Sat · Group 2)

MOTIVATION AND PARTICIPATION

Motivation: Camille demonstrates a positive attitude toward classroom activities. She shows willingness to learn, as seen in her attentiveness during storytime and her enjoyment of new routines, such as the weather and action miming, as well as the mood routine. She is open to engaging in new activities, including "A Present for Me," Family Bingo, and the Dice Game, which she particularly enjoyed. Camille is generally cooperative with the group and the teacher, though she occasionally engages in playful behavior with peers, such as with Zoé.

Participation: Camille actively participates in classroom activities, putting her acquired knowledge into practice. She could recite parts of the story, understood worksheet activities, and demonstrated memorization of vocabulary, colors, clothing items, and prepositions. Her participation is especially strong in activities she enjoys, such as "Who’s Missing" and "A Present for Me." While she sometimes holds back when less confident, as noted on a day when she was more hesitant, she responds well to encouragement and continues to engage.

BEHAVIOUR

Camille is well-integrated within the group and generally focused, though she can be playful or slightly distracting at times, such as when jokingly hiding materials instead of returning them immediately. Her behavior is influenced by the group’s mood, as the entire class occasionally became bored toward the end of the story. However, her overall conduct was praised, and she contributed positively to the group dynamic. There is no indication that external factors like weather or holidays affected her behavior.

LEARNING

Use of structures worked on during the story: Camille shows a good grasp of the structures and vocabulary from the story. She could recall parts of the story, understood worksheet activities about characters' abilities, and remembered prepositions, colors, and clothing items. However, she and the group still needed reminders for correct structures in some activities.

Level of learning objectives achieved: Camille has achieved a solid understanding of the material, demonstrating memorization and application of vocabulary and routines. She quickly adapted to new routines, such as miming weather and actions, and the mood routine ("he’s smiling because he’s happy").

Strengths:

  • Strong memorization of vocabulary, including colors, clothing, and prepositions.
  • Enthusiastic participation in interactive activities like "A Present for Me," Family Bingo, and the Dice Game.
  • Quick understanding of new routines and willingness to repeat and practice.
  • Positive attitude and attentiveness during storytime and group activities.

Weaknesses and plan for improvement:

  • Occasionally requires reminders for correct grammatical structures during activities.
  • Sometimes holds back when less confident, though she responds well to encouragement.
  • The group, including Camille, is still learning to ask questions about physical appearance before guessing identities in activities like "Who’s Missing."
The school will continue to reinforce structures and encourage Camille’s confidence in participation, particularly in areas where she is less certain.

Motivation and Participation

Camille was attentive overall and very happy to listen to the new story. She loved the Present for me activity, Who’s missing, Family Bingo and the Dice Game. She understood the worksheet activity well and did very well on the task about what Oliver and Baby could or couldn’t do.

She could repeat when asked and, although she was a bit less confident and more hesitant today, she still took part. She needed help to remember the correct structures in many activities, but she showed a real understanding and a good memorisation of the vocabulary.

Behaviour

Camille was mostly attentive, although she was a bit distracting with Zoé at times and was not always giving the material back directly when asked, hiding it jokingly. The group got bored by the end of the story. Camille was a bit less confident today and seemed more hesitant, but with encouragement she seemed quite happy.

Learning

  • Learning objectives achieved: Camille could recite parts of the story and knew parts of it well. She understood the worksheet activity very well and could do the activity about what Oliver and Baby could or couldn’t do very well.

  • Weaknesses: She is still learning to ask questions about a person’s physical appearance before asking who it is; this is a work in progress.
  • Plan for improvement and school commitment: We will continue to practise these structures and keep encouraging her.
